title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Link Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Link Line
options.lineage: Sound Transit Link and King County Metro wayfinding
options.thesis: 88 neighborhoods read as stations on one line; each station's platform is its price interval.
options.viewport: Navy nav rail; Price Prediction leads: neighborhood + guests in, full price distribution with 94% band out, and the chosen station lit yellow on the route strip beside it.
options.risk: Transit metaphor can turn decorative if the line stops encoding real posterior medians and intervals.

raised.raise: Tight type scale: rank carried by weight, case and rule, not by size jumps.
Metro yellow is reserved for the one selected station and the primary action, nowhere else.
Method notes hang in a margin column beside each chart, on 1px rules.
One neighborhood in focus at a time; the rest of the line stays quiet context.

options.label: Forecast Desk
options.thesis: A nightly price issued like a forecast: most likely value plus the fan of what could happen.
options.viewport: Slate nav; a forecast panel: 'Capitol Hill, 2 guests: $168 likely, 80% chance under $240' over a fan chart.
options.risk: Familiar: fan charts and forecast framing are a common way to dress up Bayesian demos.

options.label: Live Specimen
options.thesis: One guest-count slider remaps all 88 neighborhood price curves at once, like an axis morphing a glyph grid.
options.viewport: A giant predicted price over a grid of 88 small posterior curves that all shift as the slider moves.
options.case: Shows varying slopes vividly and wins on clarity; recruiters do not identify with type specimens.
options.risk: Streamlit reruns on slider release, so the live morph needs client-side Plotly frames.

options.label: Pulse Index
options.lineage: Factory Records sleeves, the Unknown Pleasures pulsar plot
options.thesis: 88 stacked posterior densities as white hairlines on matte black; the chosen neighborhood lifts to double weight.
options.viewport: Black field owned by the ridgeline of all neighborhoods; prediction readout set small in the corner.
options.case: Data people know the joyplot instantly; names stay as labels, but the dark poster mood weakens a working dashboard.
options.risk: Near-black with one hot accent is a look many AI dashboards fall into.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Everything at one type size on raked glass slides.
options.viewport: Slides of neighborhoods raked across a lit bed.
options.case: Raked containers fight chart reading; recruiters do not know the artifact.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case and rule instead of size.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, friendly labels, one action color.
options.viewport: Stacked cards with a bottom tab bar.
options.case: Lands on the generic card dashboard you ruled out.
options.kept: One saturated color only where something can be done.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Twin text columns round a keyed rail, notes in a wide margin.
options.viewport: A dense edition page of model notes.
options.case: Reads as the academic paper you want to avoid.
options.kept: Method notes as margin apparatus on 1px rules.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One neighborhood fills the screen, next one a flick away.
options.case: Hides comparison across neighborhoods, the core of the model.
options.kept: One neighborhood in focus at a time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light analytics dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, KPI row, prediction form and distribution chart below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other portfolio dashboard by design.
